## Rollout workers and learner workers Tülu 3 separates generation from parameter updates. Rollout workers run a policy copy with vLLM and PagedAttention; learner workers update the policy and value models. The reference policy provides the KL comparison and is not trained. ZeRO Stage 3 partitions training states so that the models fit across devices. With a synchronous schedule, generation waits while the learner updates, then the learner waits for fresh responses. Dedicated worker pools can overlap these phases: while one batch is being consumed, rollout workers prepare another. This improves utilization without making the two phases equally fast. Queued responses may come from older policy weights. The paper uses the second-latest inference batch to control this lag. A bounded lag does not guarantee on-policy data. Their sampling-policy revision and log probabilities must remain attached to them; replacing those probabilities with scores from the updated learner changes the PPO ratio. The [[00 Учебник/12 Post-training и Alignment/07 GRPO и DeepSeek-R1#offpolicy-ratios|next chapter’s ratio analysis]] explains this distinction. These are the implementation choices in [Tülu 3, §6.3](https://arxiv.org/html/2411.15124v5#S6.SS3), not requirements of every RLVR algorithm.
